name: Regularly varying tails are subexponential
scope_note: Laws on [0, infinity). The sign of the index is not assumed; it is forced.

name: Subexponential laws are long-tailed
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.IsSubexponential.tendsto_tail_sub_div {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ}
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (h : ExtremeValueTheory.IsSubexponential μ) (y : ℝ) :
  Filter.Tendsto (fun x => ExtremeValueTheory.tail μ (x - y) / ExtremeValueTheory.tail μ x)
    Filter.atTop (nhds 1)

name: Tail of the n-fold convolution is ~ n times the tail
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.IsSubexponential.tendsto_tail_convPow_div {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ}
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (h : ExtremeValueTheory.IsSubexponential μ) {n : ℕ}
  (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
  Filter.Tendsto
    (fun x =>
      ExtremeValueTheory.tail (ExtremeValueTheory.Subexp.convPow μ n) x /
        ExtremeValueTheory.tail μ x)
    Filter.atTop (nhds ↑n)

name: Tail of the maximum of n iid variables
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.tendsto_measure_max_div_tail {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ}
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (hpos : ∀ (x : ℝ), 0 < ExtremeValueTheory.tail μ x)
  (n : ℕ) :
  Filter.Tendsto
    (fun x =>
      (MeasureTheory.Measure.pi fun x => μ).real {ω | ∃ i, x < ω i} / ExtremeValueTheory.tail μ x)
    Filter.atTop (nhds ↑n)
scope_note: Needs only a positive tail; stated on the product measure.

name: Single big jump principle
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.IsSubexponential.tendsto_measure_sum_div_measure_max
  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
  (h : ExtremeValueTheory.IsSubexponential μ) {n : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
  Filter.Tendsto
    (fun x =>
      (MeasureTheory.Measure.pi fun x => μ).real {ω | x < ∑ i, ω i} /
        (MeasureTheory.Measure.pi fun x => μ).real {ω | ∃ i, x < ω i})
    Filter.atTop (nhds 1)
scope_note: Fixed n >= 1; stated on the product measure.

name: Kesten's bound
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.IsSubexponential.kesten_bound {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ}
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (h : ExtremeValueTheory.IsSubexponential μ) {ε : ℝ}
  (hε : 0 < ε) :
  ∃ K,
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ),
      ExtremeValueTheory.tail (ExtremeValueTheory.Subexp.convPow μ n) x ≤
        K * (1 + ε) ^ n * ExtremeValueTheory.tail μ x
scope_note: All n and all real x, slightly stronger than the book.

name: Subexponentiality is a property of the tail-equivalence class
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.IsSubexponential.of_tendsto_tail_div {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ}
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ}
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure ν] (h : ExtremeValueTheory.IsSubexponential μ)
  (hν0 : ν (Set.Iio 0) = 0) {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c)
  (hν :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun x => ExtremeValueTheory.tail ν x / ExtremeValueTheory.tail μ x) Filter.atTop
      (nhds c)) :
  ExtremeValueTheory.IsSubexponential ν
scope_note: The new law is on [0, infinity), and the limit c is positive.

name: Convolution powers of a subexponential law are subexponential
Compound laws of subexponential laws are subexponential
scope_note: Light-tailed counting law, E(1+eps)^N < infinity. Stated for the compound law sum p_n mu^{*n}, not for a random sum on a probability space.

name: Random sums: P(S_N > x) ~ E N P(X > x)
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.IsSubexponential.tendsto_tail_compound_div {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ}
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {p : ℕ → NNReal}
  (h : ExtremeValueTheory.IsSubexponential μ) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε)
  (hs : Summable fun n => ↑(p n) * (1 + ε) ^ n) :
  Filter.Tendsto
    (fun x =>
      ExtremeValueTheory.tail (ExtremeValueTheory.compound μ p) x / ExtremeValueTheory.tail μ x)
    Filter.atTop (nhds (∑' (n : ℕ), ↑n * ↑(p n)))
scope_note: Light-tailed counting law. Stated for the compound law, which is the law of an independent random sum.

name: Embrechts-Veraverbeke ruin asymptotics
scope_note: The ruin probability is defined by the Pollaczek-Khinchine formula, which is not derived from the Cramér-Lundberg process: the link from the risk process to the formula is not proved.

name: Ruin with regularly varying claims
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.tendsto_pkRuin_div_mul_tail {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ}
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {α : ℝ}
  (hRV : ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying (ExtremeValueTheory.tail μ) (-α)) (hα : 1 < α)
  {ρ : ℝ} (hρ : 0 < ρ) :
  Filter.Tendsto
    (fun u =>
      ExtremeValueTheory.pkRuin ρ (ExtremeValueTheory.integratedTail μ) u /
        (u * ExtremeValueTheory.tail μ u))
    Filter.atTop (nhds (1 / ((ρ * ∫ (t : ℝ) in Set.Ioi 0, ExtremeValueTheory.tail μ t) * (α - 1))))
scope_note: Same as embrechts-veraverbeke: the ruin probability is the Pollaczek-Khinchine formula, not derived from the risk process. Nonnegative claims are not assumed, so m is E X+.

name: The class S* is contained in the subexponential class
scope_note: Theorem number not verified against the paper.

name: Integrated tails of S* laws are subexponential
scope_note: Theorem number not verified against the paper.

name: Weibull-type tails exp(-x^tau), tau < 1, are subexponential
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.IsSubexponential.of_tail_eq_exp_neg_rpow {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ}
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {τ : ℝ} (h0 : μ (Set.Iio 0) = 0) (hτ0 : 0 < τ)
  (hτ1 : τ < 1) (htail : ∀ (x : ℝ), 0 ≤ x → ExtremeValueTheory.tail μ x = Real.exp (-x ^ τ)) :
  ExtremeValueTheory.IsSubexponential μ
scope_note: Takes any measure with this tail on [0, infinity); weibullTailLaw shows one exists.

name: The lognormal law is subexponential
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.IsSubexponential.lognormal (m : ℝ) {v : NNReal} (hv : v ≠ 0) :
  ExtremeValueTheory.IsSubexponential (ExtremeValueTheory.lognormal m v)

name: Closure of the subexponential class under convolution roots
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.IsSubexponential.of_convPow {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ}
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (h0 : μ (Set.Iio 0) = 0) {n : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n)
  (hG : ExtremeValueTheory.IsSubexponential (ExtremeValueTheory.Subexp.convPow μ n)) :
  ExtremeValueTheory.IsSubexponential μ

name: Tails of finite moving averages
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.LinearProcess.tendsto_measureReal_sum_mul_div.{u_1, u_2} {Ω : Type u_1}
  {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {P : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure P]
  {ι : Type u_2} {Z : ι → Ω → ℝ} {Z₀ : Ω → ℝ} (hZ : ∀ (j : ι), Measurable (Z j))
  (hZ₀ : Measurable Z₀) (hind : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun Z P)
  (hident : ∀ (j : ι), ProbabilityTheory.IdentDistrib (Z j) Z₀ P P) {α p : ℝ}
  (hL : ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying (fun x => P.real {ω | x < |Z₀ ω|}) (-α))
  (hp :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun x => P.real {ω | x < Z₀ ω} / P.real {ω | x < |Z₀ ω|}) Filter.atTop (nhds p))
  (ψ : ι → ℝ) (s : Finset ι) :
  Filter.Tendsto (fun x => P.real {ω | x < ∑ j ∈ s, ψ j * Z j ω} / P.real {ω | x < |Z₀ ω|})
    Filter.atTop (nhds (∑ j ∈ s, ExtremeValueTheory.LinearProcess.tailWeight α p (ψ j)))
scope_note: Finite sums, real coefficients, tail balance, no sign condition on the noise.

name: Tails of infinite moving averages, all alpha > 0
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.LinearProcess.tendsto_measureReal_tsum_mul_div_of_summable_rpow.{u_1}
  {Ω : Type u_1} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {P : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω}
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure P] {Z : ℕ → Ω → ℝ} {Z₀ : Ω → ℝ}
  (hZ : ∀ (j : ℕ), Measurable (Z j)) (hZ₀ : Measurable Z₀) (hind : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun Z P)
  (hident : ∀ (j : ℕ), ProbabilityTheory.IdentDistrib (Z j) Z₀ P P) {α δ p : ℝ} (hδ : 0 < δ)
  (hδα : δ < α) (hδ1 : δ < 1)
  (hL : ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying (fun x => P.real {ω | x < |Z₀ ω|}) (-α))
  (hp :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun x => P.real {ω | x < Z₀ ω} / P.real {ω | x < |Z₀ ω|}) Filter.atTop (nhds p))
  {ψ : ℕ → ℝ} (hψ : Summable fun j => |ψ j| ^ δ) :
  Filter.Tendsto (fun x => P.real {ω | x < ∑' (j : ℕ), ψ j * Z j ω} / P.real {ω | x < |Z₀ ω|})
    Filter.atTop (nhds (∑' (j : ℕ), ExtremeValueTheory.LinearProcess.tailWeight α p (ψ j)))
scope_note: Under the summability condition sum |psi_j|^delta < infinity for some delta < min(alpha, 1), that of DR85. The weaker conditions known for alpha > 1 (Mikosch-Samorodnitsky) are not covered.
